novelty_basis: Irreducibles/reducibles of Knuth's product are not in the OEIS (2026-10-18); no study of circle-product factorisation found in the C08 literature search. Elementary consequence of Arnoux's embedding; may exist in the literature on factorisation in submonoids of rings of integers.
proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C09.md Theorem 3; Weyl equidistribution), skeptic-reviewed 2026-10-18 (reviews/skeptic_C05_C08_C12.md); 0 counterexamples up to 1e6 (the Skeptic - up to 1e8), forced density 0.381967 at 1e6
statement:
If n is a circle product then nu'(n) = n psi + n* lies in (psi^3, psi^2), i.e. frac((n+1)/phi) lies in
(1/phi - psi^2, 1/phi - psi^3) = (0.2360..., 0.8541...). Hence every n with frac((n+1)/phi) outside this
interval is circle-irreducible, and these n have natural density exactly 1/phi^2 = 0.381966...
title: Window obstruction: at least a proportion 1/phi^2 of all integers are circle-irreducible
